own_solution.law: Energy balance P t = m c dT, t = m c dT / P
assumptions: all 1500 W delivered to the water (stated in the problem)

notes: Checked certified answers: base 2*4186*40/1500 = 223.253 s; m = 2.8 kg -> 468832/1500 = 312.555 s; 3.4 kg -> 569296/1500 = 379.531 s; 4.6 kg -> 770224/1500 = 513.483 s. All match. Minimal pairs hold: T2A67/T26CB and TE9F3/T4F3A share 1.4 kg and differ only in attachment. My pass-1 low rendering_not_minimal flag is withdrawn: T6174 and T160B are declared numeral-free twins of T2A67 and TE9F3, not minimal-pair variants, so the missing number is intended. Stratum differences from my pass 1 are labelling, not physics: TE9F3/T160B (add then scoop out the same mass) I called C, the authors call D; since the jug water is removed before heating it leaves no path to the heated mass, so D is defensible. TCD20/TF28B I called K (liquid regime), the authors call C via (q+dT)-q; the cancellation is correct, and all listed start temperatures 278-308 K keep the end temperature (318-348 K) below boiling, so the liquid regime is never left. The no-loss assumption is covered by the problem's wording 'delivers 1500 W to 2 kg of water'.
